evals.prompt: Our support bot in app.py parses the ticket priority and team out of the model reply with a regex, and it breaks all the time. Use xstructured so we get the customer-facing answer and a validated ticket from the same reply. Make it async and add tests that run without an API key.
evals.expected_output: app.py defines a Pydantic Ticket model with a Literal priority, wraps the chat model once with with_xstructured_output, and an async answer function awaits ainvoke and returns result.content and result.structured. A test file uses ScriptedChatModel for a valid reply and an invalid one.
assertions: The regular expression and the PRIORITY/TEAM prompt suffix are removed
A Pydantic model validates the ticket, with priority restricted to low, high, or critical
with_xstructured_output wraps the model once, outside the request function
The answer function is async and awaits ainvoke, returning result.content and result.structured
Tests use xstructured.testing.ScriptedChatModel and need no network or API key
A test checks that an invalid reply raises ParseError (or a subclass)

evals.prompt: We build a LangChain agent with create_agent and two tools. We want the agent to keep chatting normally but also hand back a validated Booking object at the end, and if the model gets the JSON wrong once it should get one chance to fix it.
evals.expected_output: Adds XStructuredMiddleware(Booking, repair_config=RepairConfig(max_attempts=1)) from xstructured.agents to the agent's middleware, keeps the tools, and reads state['structured_response'].structured after awaiting agent.ainvoke.
assertions: XStructuredMiddleware is imported from xstructured.agents and passed in middleware=[...]
The existing tools stay on the agent unchanged
Repair is bounded with RepairConfig(max_attempts=1) and no separate repair model is passed to the middleware
The validated value is read from state["structured_response"].structured
Installation uses the xstructured[agents] extra

evals.prompt: Our FastAPI endpoint streams an LLM answer over server-sent events. Product wants the prose to appear token by token and then a status card rendered from typed fields once they're ready, all from one model call.
evals.expected_output: Wraps the model with with_xstructured_output and iterates wrapper.astream(...), forwarding TEXT_DELTA text as it arrives and sending the card on STRUCTURED_END (or RESULT), without a second model call.
assertions: The endpoint iterates astream() on the xstructured wrapper itself, not on a composed chain
TEXT_DELTA events are forwarded as prose as they arrive
The card is built from event.structured on STRUCTURED_END or from event.result on RESULT
Only one model call is made per request
Repair is not relied on while streaming events

evals.prompt: Since we started passing a ChatPromptTemplate into our xstructured wrapper we get `TypeError: Cannot add xstructured instructions to input of type dict`. How do we fix it properly?
evals.expected_output: Explains that the template's input dict cannot carry instructions, and either ends the chain with XStructuredOutputParser and puts get_format_instructions() in the template, or wraps the prompt | model chain with inject_instructions=False and includes wrapper.instructions in the template.
assertions: Identifies that the wrapper received the template's input dict rather than messages
Proposes XStructuredOutputParser with get_format_instructions() in the template, or inject_instructions=False with wrapper.instructions in the prompt
Does not suggest catching and ignoring the TypeError
Keeps schema validation unchanged
